prints.event: Canada Consumer Price Index, September (Statistics Canada)
prints.read: Only matters to US futures through the energy-inflation read-across; a hot headline would echo last week's US CPI and lean on the front end.

Builder sentiment is already deep in contraction after a three-point drop in September; another dip is expected with the 10-year above 5%, so only a print under 30 or a bounce back above 32 moves anything.
Bill stops read the front end's view of the October 28 meeting; a 26-week stop well above the 13-week keeps the December hike priced.

prints.event: China GDP, third quarter (NBS, released Sunday evening CT)
prints.read: A small beat on the year-on-year rate, with the quarter-on-quarter pace at 1.2% against 1.1% expected, enough to steady Asia and lift US futures but not a growth story on its own.
In line; factory output is holding up while property investment is down 20.6% year to date.
The clearest beat of the batch, though a 1% consumer is still weak and the fixed-asset investment line stayed at minus 7.2% year to date.

read.call: A relief bounce after the worst week since June, with S&P futures up about 0.7% and Nasdaq futures up about 1.3% on the China beat and Brent off 1.5% to 2%, but no US data to anchor it, so the chip tape and oil decide whether it holds.
read.swing: Oil: Brent near $107 after a tanker hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz and the White House waived some Russia sanctions; a move back above $110 reverses the bounce and puts the 10-year back toward 5.3%.
drivers: Friday's selloff was AI financing, not macro: CoreWeave fell 12% with more than $51bn of debt, the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell an eighth straight day, the Nasdaq lost 4.5% on the week.
Rates: the 10-year sits near 5.07% to 5.09% after spiking to 5.33% on Wednesday's CPI; Treasuries extended their rally overnight as oil slipped.
Fed: blackout started Saturday ahead of the October 27-28 meeting; FedWatch prices about a 16-17% chance of an October hike and roughly 89-90% for December from the current 3.75-4.00% range.
China: Q3 GDP 4.5% and retail sales 1.1% both beat, the yuan hit 6.68, its strongest since July 2022, supportive for risk at the margin.
The US calendar is empty of hard data all week; the only scheduled items are housing (NAHB today, starts tomorrow), claims Thursday and flash PMIs Friday, so earnings carry the tape.

what_mattered.headline: China Q3 GDP beat and retail sales doubled expectations
what_mattered.fact: GDP 4.5% y/y vs 4.4% consensus (q/q 1.2% vs 1.1%); September retail sales 1.1% vs 0.5%; industrial output 5.5% in line; property investment -20.6% year to date.
what_mattered.implication: Enough to lift Nasdaq futures about 1.3% in Asian hours and firm the yuan; the property line says the floor, not an upturn.

what_mattered.headline: Oil fell on a Russia sanctions waiver despite a Hormuz mine strike
what_mattered.fact: Brent down about 1.5% to 2% overnight to roughly $107-108 after settling at $109.86 Friday (+4.9% on the week); Iran said a tanker hit a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz; tanker rates at record highs.
what_mattered.implication: Oil is the inflation channel the Fed is reacting to (September CPI energy +5.2% m/m); a lower open in crude is why Treasuries rallied and futures are green.

what_mattered.headline: Friday: Nasdaq -2.1%, S&P -1.1%, led by chips and AI credit
what_mattered.fact: S&P 500 7,659.44 (-1.9% on the week, worst since June), Nasdaq 26,140.03 (-4.5% on the week), Russell 2000 -1.7%; Micron -5.6%, Intel -5.8%, CoreWeave -12%.
what_mattered.implication: The selloff is about AI capex financing and the cost of capital at a 5% 10-year, which makes Meta's Wednesday capex guide the week's real macro event.

what_mattered.headline: Warsh gave no rate guidance; October hike odds fell to about 17%
what_mattered.fact: At the IMF meeting in Bangkok Chair Warsh said the Fed is 'not in that business anymore' on forward guidance; CME FedWatch 17% for an October hike (from 28%), 89% for December; 10-year about 5.09%, had spiked to 5.33% after CPI.
what_mattered.implication: The blackout freezes Fed talk until October 28, so rates trade on oil and auctions this week, with Wednesday's $13bn 20-year reopening the test of the Treasury rally.

what_mattered.headline: Last week's inflation and sentiment backdrop
what_mattered.fact: September CPI +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y (core 2.6%); September payrolls +29k, unemployment 4.2%; Michigan preliminary October sentiment 46.3 vs 48.1, 1-year inflation expectations 4.7%, long-run 3.5%.
what_mattered.implication: Hot headline inflation on energy with a soft labor market and sour consumers is the stagflation setup the market is pricing into a December hike; GDPNow still has Q3 at 3.6%.

look_at: Brent against $110 at the US open: it drove Friday's late rally in energy and the overnight bond bid, and a reversal higher is the fastest way to lose the futures gain.
Semiconductors and CoreWeave at the open: the Philadelphia semiconductor index has fallen eight sessions running and whether it bounces with futures tells you if Friday was capitulation or a pause.
The 10-year around 5.07%: a close back under 5.05% with oil soft would confirm the Treasury rally; the $13bn 20-year reopening Wednesday is the real test.
NAHB at 09:00 CT: the only US print; a sub-30 reading would be the lowest since 2012 and feed the growth-scare side of the stagflation trade.

Bank earnings today (Fifth Third, Zions, Western Alliance) for credit and deposit cost commentary after a 25 bp hike cycle restart; Netflix Tuesday and Meta, Tesla, Texas Instruments and Lam Wednesday are where AI capex gets re-priced.

fed.market_pricing: Target range 3.75-4.00% after the September 16 hike. CME FedWatch about 17% for a 25 bp hike on October 28 (hold about 83-84%), roughly 89-90% for a December hike (Yahoo/Investopedia Oct 16, FXStreet Oct 19). Blackout began Saturday October 17.
